Fit a zero-inflated spatial autoregressive (ZISAR) model

Source: R/zisar.R
zisar.Rd

Fits the ZISAR model of Salvini, Arbia and Nardelli (2026): a zero-inflated negative binomial model whose log-mean follows a simultaneous autoregressive (SAR) process with unit-level random effects. By default the inflation probability depends on covariates only (the restricted model); zero_spatial adds spatial structure to it (the general model). zisar() takes a two-part formula and a data frame; zisar_fit() is the matrix interface underneath it.

Usage

zisar(
  formula,
  data,
  W,
  zero_spatial = c("none", "reduced", "field", "sar"),
  basis = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  logdet = c("auto", "eigen", "sparse"),
  restarts = TRUE,
  control = list(),
  silent = TRUE
)

zisar_fit(
  y,
  X,
  Z = NULL,
  W,
  offset = NULL,
  zero_spatial = c("none", "reduced", "field", "sar"),
  basis = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  logdet = c("auto", "eigen", "sparse"),
  restarts = TRUE,
  control = list(),
  silent = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: the terms before | enter the count process, those after it the zero-inflation process. Without |, both processes use the same terms. Use | 1 for a constant inflation probability. An offset() term in the count part enters the log-mean with coefficient one.

data

A data frame with one row per spatial unit, in the order of the rows of W. Missing values are not allowed: every unit enters the spatial multiplier, so none can be dropped.

W

Spatial weights: an \(n \times n\) matrix (base or sparse 'Matrix') or an spdep listw object, with zero diagonal and preferably row-standardised.

zero_spatial

Inflation predictor: "none" (restricted model), "reduced", "field" or "sar"; see Model. FALSE and TRUE stand for "none" and "field".

basis

For zero_spatial = "reduced", the basis from zisar_basis().

fixed

Optional named list of parameters held at fixed values: rho, kappa, sigma, rho0 and sigma0 (scalars, natural scale), beta (length ncol(X)) or gamma (length ncol(Z)). In beta and gamma, NA entries are estimated.

start

Optional named list of starting values, with the same names and scales as fixed. Defaults: beta from a Poisson regression, inflation intercept from the share of zeros, rho = 0, kappa = 1, sigma = 0.5, rho0 = 0 and, for the fields, rho0 and sigma0 from the grid described in Estimation. To restart from a previous fit, use start = list(beta = coef(fit, "count"), gamma = coef(fit, "zero"), rho = fit$rho, kappa = fit$kappa, sigma = fit$sigma).

logdet

Method for the log-determinant: "auto", "eigen" or "sparse". See Estimation.

restarts

If TRUE, restart a fit that fails the checks described in Estimation. Set it to FALSE when a single fit is slow and a large gradient is expected.

control

List of control parameters for stats::nlminb(), merged with the defaults eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 500, rel.tol = 1e-10.

silent

If FALSE, print the 'TMB' tracing output.

y

Vector of non-negative integer counts.

X

Design matrix of the count process, \(n \times p\); include a column of ones for an intercept.

Z

Design matrix of the zero-inflation process, \(n \times q\). NULL gives an intercept only.

offset

Optional vector of length \(n\) added to the count log-mean (for example the log of an exposure).

Value

An object of class "zisar", a list with, among others:

coefficients

List with the count (\(\beta\)) and zero (\(\gamma\)) coefficients.

rho, kappa, sigma

Spatial autoregressive parameter, negative binomial shape and random-effect standard deviation.

zero_spatial

The inflation predictor, as in the argument.

rho0, sigma0

Parameters of the inflation field or filter; NULL when absent.

eta

Mode of the latent field \(\eta\) given the data.

g

Mode of the inflation field (\(g\), or \(B\alpha\) for the reduced-rank field); zero without a field.

zeta

The inflation predictor, \(\mathrm{logit}(\pi)\).

fitted.values

Fitted means \(E[y_i] = (1 - \pi_i)\mu_i\).

loglik

Laplace-approximated marginal log-likelihood.

field_profile

For the fields: the grid of \((\rho_0, \sigma_0)\) with the gain in log-likelihood over the restricted fit, and the restricted log-likelihood.

convergence, message

Convergence code and message of stats::nlminb().

max_grad, laplace_ok

Largest gradient component at the optimum, and whether the optimum passed the checks described in Estimation.

tmb

The 'TMB' object, for advanced use.

Use the methods summary(), coef(), vcov(), logLik(), predict(), residuals() and zisar_effects() rather than the components directly.

Model

For units \(i = 1, \dots, n\) linked by a spatial weights matrix \(W\), $$\eta = \rho W \eta + X\beta + u, \qquad u \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I),$$ so that \(\eta = (I - \rho W)^{-1}(X\beta + u)\). Each count is zero with probability \(\pi_i\) (a structural zero) and otherwise negative binomial, $$y_i \sim \pi_i \, 1\{y_i = 0\} + (1 - \pi_i)\, \mathrm{NB}(\mu_i, \kappa), \qquad \mu_i = \exp(\eta_i + o_i), \qquad \mathrm{logit}(\pi_i) = \zeta_i,$$ with \(\mathrm{Var}(y_i \mid \text{not a structural zero}) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\kappa\) and \(o_i\) an optional offset (log exposure). The offset scales unit \(i\) only: it does not pass through the spatial multiplier.

The inflation predictor \(\zeta\) is set by zero_spatial:

"none"

The restricted model, \(\zeta = Z\gamma\).

"reduced"

A reduced-rank SAR field, \(\zeta = Z\gamma + B\alpha\) with \(\alpha = \rho_0 W_K \alpha + e_0\), \(e_0 \sim N(0, \sigma_0^2 I_K)\): \(\alpha\) holds the values of the field at the \(K\) knots of a lattice, \(W_K\) is the contiguity of the knots and \(B\) a basis of local functions built by zisar_basis(), so that structural zeros can cluster in space beyond what the covariates explain. \(\rho_0 \ge 0\). This is the recommended general model.

"field"

A SAR field with one element per unit, \(\zeta = Z\gamma + g\) with \(g = \rho_0 W g + e_0\), \(e_0 \sim N(0, \sigma_0^2 I)\). Its Laplace approximation fails (see Estimation).

"sar"

A SAR filter on the predictor, \(\zeta = (I - \rho_0 W)^{-1} Z\gamma\): the covariates of a unit's neighbours shift its inflation probability. No random effects are added.

The random fields are independent of \(u\). The restricted model is the limit \(\sigma_0 \to 0\) of the fields, and \(\rho_0 = 0\) of the filter.

Estimation

The latent field \(\eta\) (and \(g\) or \(\alpha\)) is integrated out with the Laplace approximation in 'TMB', and the marginal likelihood is maximised with stats::nlminb() over \((\beta, \gamma, \rho, \kappa, \sigma)\) and, in the general model, \(\rho_0\) and \(\sigma_0\), with \(\rho = \tanh(\rho_{raw})\) restricted to \((-1, 1)\). Standard errors come from the inverse Hessian of the Laplace objective; those of \(\rho\), \(\kappa\), \(\sigma\), \(\rho_0\) and \(\sigma_0\) from the delta method.

With a random field in the inflation predictor ("reduced" or "field"), the restricted model is fitted first, the Laplace likelihood of the general model is evaluated on a grid of \((\rho_0, \sigma_0)\) with the other parameters at the restricted estimates, and the optimiser starts from the best grid point. The grid and the gain over the restricted fit are returned in field_profile; a gain that never rises above zero means the data hold no field.

The unit-level field ("field") defeats the Laplace approximation: each \(g_i\) is informed by a single outcome that is zero or not, and the error of the approximation accumulates over the \(n\) elements of the field. On data without a field the approximate likelihood rises with \(\sigma_0\), and the likelihood-ratio statistic against the restricted model can reach thousands. Use "reduced", whose knot values are each informed by many units, and check any general fit on data simulated without a field (simulate() of the restricted fit).

Each fit is checked: when the optimiser does not converge, or the optimum has a gradient above 0.01 or a positive log-likelihood, the fit is restarted from three other values of \(\kappa\) and \(\sigma\) and from up to three random perturbations of the best point (this uses the random number generator; restarts = FALSE skips it). If no clean optimum is found, zisar() warns and laplace_ok is FALSE. A positive log-likelihood is always a spurious optimum of the approximation. A large gradient is not specific: it marks spurious optima, but it also appears at genuine optima when structural zeros occur among units of high intensity, since the conditional distribution of \(\eta_i\) of a zero unit then has two modes and the objective is not smooth. Fit the model to data simulated from the fit to tell the two apart, and use a parametric bootstrap (simulate() and refits started from the estimates) for standard errors.

The log-determinant \(\log|I - \rho W|\) is computed either from the eigenvalues of \(W\), found once in \(O(n^3)\) time and \(O(n^2)\) memory (logdet = "eigen"), or from a sparse Cholesky factorisation of \((I - \rho W)'(I - \rho W)\) at each evaluation (logdet = "sparse"), which scales to tens of thousands of units. "auto" uses the sparse method when \(n > 5000\). The knot field uses the eigenvalues of \(W_K\).

Nested models

fixed holds parameters at given values, which gives the special cases of the model: fixed = list(rho = 0) is the aspatial zero-inflated negative binomial with random effects (ZINB-RE), and with an intercept-only inflation part (y ~ x | 1), fixed = list(gamma = -20) sets \(\pi_i \approx 0\), the SAR negative binomial with random effects (SAR-NB-RE). Likelihood-ratio tests between nested fits use logLik(). The restricted model sits on the boundary of the models with a field (\(\sigma_0 = 0\)), so the likelihood-ratio statistic between them does not have the usual chi-squared distribution: its p-value from \(\chi^2_2\) is conservative.

References

Salvini, N., Arbia, G. and Nardelli, V. (2026). ZISAR: A zero-inflated spatial autoregressive model for count data with random effects. Working paper, Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore.

Kristensen, K., Nielsen, A., Berg, C. W., Skaug, H. and Bell, B. M. (2016). TMB: Automatic differentiation and Laplace approximation. Journal of Statistical Software, 70(5), 1–21. doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i05

See also

zisar_effects() for direct, indirect and total effects, zisar_basis() for the reduced-rank field, rzisar() to simulate from the model.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- rzisar(12, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8))
fit <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zisar(formula = y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
#> 
#> 144 spatial units, 38.9% zeros
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (SAR negative binomial, log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)   1.6222     0.8087   2.006   0.0449 *  
#> x1            0.6690     0.1141   5.865 4.49e-09 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial, logit link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
#> (Intercept)  -0.8054     0.2642  -3.048  0.00230 **
#> z1            0.6516     0.2243   2.905  0.00367 **
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Spatial and dispersion parameters:
#>       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> rho     0.1056     0.4121   0.256    0.798
#> kappa   1.4609     0.8026                 
#> sigma   0.2034     0.6278                 
#> 
#> Log-likelihood (Laplace): -344.303 on 7 Df
#> AIC: 702.606   BIC: 723.394
#> Log-determinant: eigen.  Optimiser: converged after 24 iterations.
#> 

# Aspatial ZINB with random effects, and a likelihood-ratio test of rho = 0
fit0 <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W,
              fixed = list(rho = 0))
lr <- 2 * (logLik(fit) - logLik(fit0))
pchisq(as.numeric(lr), df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
#> [1] 0.8091071

# \donttest{
# General model: zeros clustered by a spatial field of their own, fitted
# with a reduced-rank field on knots 4 cells apart
set.seed(2)
sim2 <- rzisar(20, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8),
               zero_spatial = "field", rho0 = 0.9, sigma0 = 0.5)
b <- zisar_basis(sim2$coords, h = 4)
fit2 <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim2$data, W = sim2$W,
              zero_spatial = "reduced", basis = b)
summary(fit2)
#> 
#> Call:
